Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::size¶

Back to Timeline Index Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

std::int64_t Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::size() const

What It Does¶

Returns how many timestamps are stored in the index.

This is the case-axis length. If you are resampling, joining, slicing, or aligning another object against a Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor, this is the number of original observations on that axis.

In practice, size() is the first integrity check before you attach an independent payload to the axis.

Returns¶

std::int64_t The number of timestamps in the index.

Examples¶

Example 1. Basic length check before resampling external values.

auto idx = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-11-01T00:00:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:20:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T00:40:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T01:00:00Z",
    "2024-11-01T01:20:00Z",
}).index();

auto n = idx.size();
std::cout << "n = " << n << "\n";

Output¶

n = 5

Example 2. Guard that a values vector matches the index length.

auto values = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{12.0, 18.0, 15.0, 22.0});
if (values.numel() != idx.size()) {
    throw std::runtime_error("values must line up with the index");
}

Notes¶

  • size() is equivalent to the number of cases on the time axis.

  • If a values object does not agree with size(), the problem is almost always misalignment at construction time rather than later in the pipeline.

  • It is often the first sanity check before calling resample_sum, resample_mean, or rolling_sum.

See Also¶

  • Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::host: materialize the underlying epoch-nanosecond ticks on the host.

  • Timeline::TimelineIndexAccessor::timeline: expose the underlying Timeline.
